newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU shows outstanding trade growth with 'three Chinas'.
newsitem.headline: EU shows outstanding trade growth with 'three Chinas'.

text.p: European Union trade with the "three Chinas" -- mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan -- has soared this decade, showing growth of over 16 percent a year since 1990.

Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, said on Tuesday that exports from the 15-nation bloc to China, Taiwan and Hong Kong rose from 18.2 billion European currency units (ecus) in 1990 to 41.9 billion last year.
Imports rose from 27.9 billion ecus to 50.1 billion, leaving the EU some 8.14 billion in the red. The trade deficit in 1990 was 9.8 billion ecus.
Year-on-year, EU imports from Hong Kong, China and Taiwan last year rose 0.3 percent, 13.8 percent and 9.7 percent respectively.
Exports to Hong Kong and China rose 9.8 and 0.2 percent, but fell 1.7 percent to Taiwan.
Manufactured goods -- chiefly machinery and transport equipment -- accounted for nearly 90 percent of EU exports to Hongkong and also for over 31 percent of imports from the British colony.
Electrical goods and automatic data-processing equipment were the biggest EU imports, accounting for nearly two-thirds of the total. Clothing and accessories accounted for nearly 35 percent.
